blocks.text: The sense of smell (olfaction) comes from chemoreceptors high in the nasal cavities. These receptors are the ends of sensory neurons in a thin tissue, the nasal epithelium, packed between supporting cells, which protect them, and basal cells, which act as stem cells to replace old neurons.

items: The dendrites of these neurons end in tiny hair-like cilia that project into the moist mucus lining the nasal cavity.
Airborne chemicals dissolve in the mucus and bind to specific receptor sites on the cilia.
The binding creates impulses that travel along the olfactory nerves (cranial nerve I) to the olfactory bulb.

blocks.alt: A head in section with the nasal epithelium marked in the roof of the nasal cavity, and an enlargement of it: axons of the olfactory nerve pass up from sensory neurons that lie between support cells, with a row of basal cells; the dendrites end in cilia in the mucus, among odour molecules.
